name: Grenada
headline: Grenada: +4.8% growth in 2025, 0.6% inflation, debt 69% of GDP
sections: Grenada is a $1.5 billion economy (2025), the world's 199th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.8% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $21K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 3.3% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 0.6% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 2.6% in 2022.
Gross government debt is 69% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 90% in 2020. The general government balance is −5.0% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −23.1% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Net FDI inflows were 12.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 64% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 75.4 years (2024). Population: 116 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
